A.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a wave, which does not change when waves cross. Superposition combines the instantaneous values, not the maxima.

B.explanation: The principle of superposition states the resultant displacement at a point is the vector sum of the individual displacements, $x = x_1 + x_2$.

C.explanation: Frequency is set by each source and is unchanged by superposition. Waves pass through each other without changing $f$.

D.explanation: Wave velocity is set by the medium and is unchanged by superposition. Velocities of the two waves are not added.

hints: Notice the question says superpose at a point at one instant, so think about the displacement of the medium there and then, not a whole-wave maximum.
Recall that amplitude means maximum displacement while displacement at a point can be positive, negative or zero and changes with time.
Connect this to interference: to decide if you get constructive reinforcement or destructive cancellation you must add the signed displacements using $x = x_1 + x_2$.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: two waves meet at the same point in a medium, so consider the disturbance of the medium at that place and instant.
State the governing rule: the principle of superposition says the resultant displacement is the vector sum of the separate displacements, $x = x_1 + x_2$, taking sign into account.
Distinguish the terms: amplitude is the fixed maximum $|x|_{max}$ for each wave, while displacement varies moment to moment, so it is the displacements that add and can reinforce or cancel.
Check the other quantities: frequency $f$ is fixed by the source and wave speed $v$ is fixed by the medium, so neither is added when waves cross.
Applying the vector addition of displacements gives constructive or destructive resultant at that point. This is option B
